nav.label: Main menu
login.title: Sign in
login.blocked: Too many failed attempts. Try again in a few minutes.
setup.title: First-time setup
setup.intro: Choose the password for this administration interface.
setup.token_hint: The token was written to the server log when the relay started. The server administrator can look it up.
setup.bad_token: The setup token is not correct.
setup.too_short: The password must be at least 12 characters.
dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.ms_missing: The Microsoft 365 connection is not configured, so no mail can be sent.
dashboard.secret_expired: The client secret has expired. No mail can be sent until you enter a new one.
dashboard.secret_soon: The client secret expires in %d day(s). Renew it before it expires.
clients.title: Clients
clients.intro: Every device that sends mail needs a fixed IP address and its own login. Both must match.
clients.name: Name
clients.add_hint: A password is generated and shown once. Use a single IP address (192.168.1.50) or a network (192.168.1.0/24).
created.once: Copy these settings now. The password is shown only once and cannot be retrieved later.
created.sender_hint: The sender address on the device must be an existing mailbox in your Microsoft 365 tenant.
created.cert_hint: The relay uses a self-signed certificate by default. If the device refuses it, turn off certificate validation on the device.
devices.title: Unknown devices
devices.intro: These IP addresses tried to connect but are not registered. If one of them is a device you want to allow, add it as a client.
devices.none: No unknown devices in the last 30 days.
logs.title: Logs
logs.retention: Events are kept for %d days. Message contents are never logged.
reason.user_wrong_ip: Login from the wrong IP address
reason.auth_blocked: Blocked after too many failed logins
hint.ip_not_allowed: A device with this IP address tried to connect. If it is yours, give it a fixed IP address and add it on the Clients page. If you do not recognise it, restrict the SMTP port in your firewall.
hint.auth_required: The device connected but tried to send without signing in. Turn on SMTP authentication on the device.
hint.unknown_user: The username does not exist or the client is disabled. Check the username on the device against the Clients page.
hint.bad_password: The password is wrong. Reset the password on the Clients page and enter the new one on the device.
hint.user_wrong_ip: The login is valid but the device connected from another IP address than the one registered. The device probably received a new address: set a fixed IP address, or change the IP address of the client.
hint.auth_blocked: This IP address made too many failed login attempts and is blocked for a few minutes. Fix the credentials on the device.
hint.no_sender: The device sent an empty sender address. Set a sender (From) address on the device.
hint.no_recipients: The message had no recipient. Check the address entered on the device.
hint.message_too_large: The message is larger than the configured limit (SMTPRELAY_MAX_MESSAGE_MB). Scan at a lower resolution or raise the limit.
hint.graph_auth_failed: Microsoft refused the relay's app sign-in. The client secret is probably wrong or expired, or the connection is not configured. Open the Microsoft 365 page and use Check connection.
hint.graph_forbidden: The app is not allowed to send as this mailbox. Check admin consent for Mail.Send and, if you use Exchange RBAC scoping, that the sender mailbox is in scope. Role changes can take up to 30 minutes.
hint.graph_mailbox_not_found: The sender address is not a mailbox in your tenant. Use an existing mailbox (a shared mailbox is fine) as the sender address on the device.
hint.graph_rejected: Microsoft rejected the message itself (for example an invalid address or content). Check the technical detail.
hint.graph_temporary: Microsoft is throttling or temporarily unavailable. The device may retry; if it does not, send again later.
hint.internal_error: The relay hit an unexpected error. Check the technical detail or ask the server administrator for the server log.
hint.message_read_failed: The message could not be read completely, for example because the connection was interrupted.
ms.title: Microsoft 365 connection
ms.check_ok: Microsoft accepted the tenant ID, client ID and client secret.
ms.wait_hint: Just set up the connection, consent or permissions? Microsoft needs about 5 minutes (sometimes up to 30) to apply them. Wait a few minutes before testing and try again. The failure is also recorded on the Logs page.
ms.setup_intro: Create an app registration in Microsoft Entra ID with the Graph permission Mail.Send, then enter its values here.
ms.secret_keep: Leave empty to keep the stored secret.
ms.expires_hint: Optional, but recommended: the dashboard warns you 30 days before the secret expires.
test.title: Send a test mail
test.intro: Sends one message through Microsoft 365 with the saved connection. This tests the Microsoft side only, not the devices.
test.from_hint: Must be an existing mailbox in your tenant, for example the shared mailbox the devices will use.
test.bad_address: Enter a plain e-mail address in both fields.
test.body: This is a test message from office-smtprelay.
account.title: Account
account.wrong_current: The current password is not correct.
account.signout_note: Changing the password signs out all other sessions.
help.title: Help
flash.client_exists: A client with this name or username already exists.
flash.client_invalid: Check the name, the IP address (or network) and the username.
flash.internal: An internal error occurred. Ask the server administrator for the server log.
flash.ms_saved: Connection saved. Use Check connection to validate it. Wait about 5 minutes before testing: Microsoft needs time to apply new permissions.
flash.ms_bad_date: The expiry date is not valid (use YYYY-MM-DD).
flash.ms_invalid: Check the tenant ID, client ID and secret.
reason.policy_test: Rule hit in test mode (not blocked)
hint.sender_not_allowed: The device used a sender address that its rules do not allow, so the message was refused. Open the client's rules and either add the address, or choose 'rewrite the sender' so the message is sent anyway with the correct address.
hint.rcpt_not_allowed: The device tried to mail an address outside what its rules allow (for example an external address while only internal recipients are allowed). Change the recipient rule of this client if this is wanted.
hint.limit_exceeded: The device reached one of its limits (messages per hour or day, recipients per message or message size). The device may retry later. Raise the limit in the client's rules if this is normal use.
hint.client_blocked: The device sent more than its limit allows and is blocked for a few minutes. You can lift the block on the client's rules page. If this is normal use, raise the limit.
hint.paused: Sending was paused with the emergency stop. Devices are told to try again later. Resume sending from the dashboard.
hint.policy_test: A rule would have blocked this message, but the rule is in test mode, so it was sent anyway. See the detail. If this is unwanted, adjust the rule; if it is normal, you can switch the rule to 'enforce'.
clients.preset_recommended: Recommended: limits, internal recipients in test mode
clients.preset_strict: Strict: limits, internal recipients only, one sender
clients.preset_hint: Presets only fill in the rules; you can change each one afterwards. With a sender mailbox, 'Recommended' rewrites every sender to that address (never refuses a device) and 'Strict' only allows that address. Without one, no sender rule is set.
settings.domains_hint: Used by the rule 'only internal recipients'. List your own mail domains.
flash.paused: Sending is paused. Devices are told to try again later.
dashboard.paused: Sending is paused (emergency stop). No mail is being delivered.
dashboard.client_blocked: Device %s is temporarily blocked because it reached its sending limit.
dashboard.test_hits: %d message(s) in the last 7 days would have been blocked by a rule in test mode (they were sent anyway).
dashboard.stop_hint: Pauses all sending at once, for example if you suspect misuse. Devices get a 'try again later' answer and nothing is lost on their side. You can resume at any time.
edit.intro: All rules are optional. Nothing is blocked until you switch a rule on. Use test mode first to see what the device really sends: violations are then only logged, not refused.
edit.blocked: This device is blocked until %s because it reached its sending limit.
edit.pattern_hint: One per line (or comma separated). Use a full address, '@domain.com' for a whole domain.
edit.sender_hint: Controls which From address this device may use. Many printers cannot set their sender: 'rewrite' accepts every message and replaces the sender, so nothing is ever refused.
edit.sender_action: If the sender is not allowed
edit.sender_rewrite_opt: Rewrite the sender to the address below (never refuses)
edit.sender_reject_opt: Refuse the message (only the allowed addresses)
edit.rcpt_hint: Controls who this device may mail. 'Only internal' keeps scan-to-mail inside your organisation, so a hijacked device cannot send spam outside.
edit.rcpt_internal: Only my own domains (plus the extra list below)
edit.limits_hint: Caps the volume of this device. A runaway or hijacked device is stopped before it can do harm. Keep limits generous.
edit.lim_empty: Leave a field empty for no limit. Limits are counted per device and reset when the relay restarts.
edit.lim_reject: Answer 'try again later' for that message
edit.lim_block_opt: Block the whole device for a while
edit.headers_hint: Optional changes applied to every message of this device.
edit.subject_tag: Prefix for the subject (for example Printer)
edit.addresses_hint: One or more addresses or networks, separated by commas (192.168.1.50, 192.168.1.64/28). Give the device a fixed IP address in your router first.
edit.access_hint: Disable the device to stop it from sending without deleting it. A new password is shown once; enter it on the device.
edit.danger_hint: The device can no longer send. Its history stays in the logs.
settings.title: General settings
settings.intro: Settings that apply to the whole relay, not to one device.
hint.attachment_not_allowed: The message contained an attachment type that the rules of this device do not allow (see the detail for the file name), so it was refused. Change the attachment rule on the device's Message tab if this file type is normal for the device.
edit.bcc_hint: Every message of this device is also delivered to these addresses (one per line, at most 10), without the recipients seeing it. Handy as an archive of scans.
edit.attach_hint: Limits which file types a device may send. Messages that break the rule are refused as a whole; attachments are never removed silently.
edit.attach_block: Refuse these file types (everything else is allowed)
edit.attach_allow: Only allow these file types (everything else is refused)
edit.attach_exts_hint: Extensions without a dot, separated by commas, for example pdf, jpg, png. The presets block programs and scripts such as exe, bat, js and ps1.
notify.title: Notifications
notify.intro: Get a short e-mail when something needs your attention, so you do not have to watch the dashboard.
notify.from_hint: Must be an existing mailbox in your Microsoft 365 tenant that the relay is allowed to send as, for example the printer mailbox.
notify.which: What do you want to hear about?
notify.kind_ms_error_hint: A message could not be delivered through Microsoft (expired secret, permissions, unknown mailbox). At most one mail per problem every 6 hours.
notify.kind_secret_expiry_hint: 30, 7 and 1 day before the secret expires, and when it has expired. Needs the expiry date on the Microsoft 365 page.
notify.kind_client_blocked_hint: A device reached its sending limit and was blocked (see the Limits tab of the device).
notify.kind_paused_hint: When someone uses the emergency stop or resumes sending.
notify.invalid: Enter a valid recipient address and sender mailbox.
notify.test_hint: Sends one message with the saved settings, so you know it arrives.
notify.test_ok: Test notification sent. Check your mailbox.
notify.test_failed: The test notification could not be sent: %s
notify.limits: Notifications are sent through Microsoft 365 itself. If the connection to Microsoft is down, an alert about that cannot be delivered, so the dashboard and Logs remain the place to look.
reason.connection_limit: Too many connections from one address
hint.connection_limit: This IP address already had the maximum number of open connections, so a new one was refused. Devices normally retry on their own. Raise the limit under Settings, General if this is normal.
settings.general_hint: Changes apply immediately, without restarting the relay. Leave a field empty to use the server default.
settings.conns: Open connections per address (0 = no limit)
settings.empty_default: The grey number in an empty field is the default that then applies.
settings.conns_hint: A limit protects the relay against a device that opens connections without end. A value of 5 to 10 is plenty for printers.
settings.env_only: The server name and the port are set during installation on the server (SMTPRELAY_HOSTNAME, SMTPRELAY_PUBLIC_SMTP_PORT). Changing them needs a restart.
settings.general_invalid: Check the values: days 1 to 3650, size 1 to 150 MB, connections 0 to 1000.
hint.tls_required: The device tried to sign in without TLS on the listener without encryption, but its rules do not allow that. Turn on TLS (STARTTLS) on the device. Only if the device cannot do TLS at all, allow it on the device's Connection tab.
flash.conn_cert_saved: The certificate was replaced and is used for new connections right away.
edit.conn_hint: By default a device must use TLS (STARTTLS) before it can sign in. Only change this for old devices that cannot do that.
edit.conn_min: Oldest TLS version this device may use
edit.conn_min_hint: Lower only for a device that cannot do TLS 1.2. Older versions are weaker, so keep this to the one device that needs it.
edit.conn_plain: This device cannot use TLS at all: let it sign in without encryption
edit.conn_plain_hint: Works only on the optional listener without encryption (Connection page). The password then travels readable over the network, so use it only on a trusted network and keep the IP address restricted.
conn.title: Connection and certificate
conn.intro: The certificate devices see, the oldest TLS version that is accepted, and extra SMTP ports. Changes apply at once.
conn.cert_expired: The certificate has expired. Devices that check certificates will refuse to connect. Create a new one or upload a valid one.
conn.cert_soon: The certificate expires within 30 days. Replace it in time.
conn.src_env: Set during installation on the server (SMTPRELAY_TLS_CERT)
conn.selfsigned_hint: A self-signed certificate is encrypted but not trusted by anyone. Most printers accept it, or let you turn certificate checking off. If a device insists on a trusted certificate, upload one from your own certificate authority.
conn.cert_managed: The certificate was set during installation on the server, so it cannot be changed here.
conn.upload_hint: The certificate and key are checked before anything changes. The key is stored in the data volume of the relay.
conn.regen_names: Names and IP addresses it is valid for
conn.regen_hint: Comma separated, for example the server name and the fixed IP address devices connect to.
conn.min_hint: Devices that only know older TLS versions are refused unless you lower this. Prefer to lower it for one device only, on that device's Connection tab.
conn.min_warn: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are outdated. Use them only for old devices on a trusted network.
conn.ports_hint: The normal port (%s, STARTTLS) is always active. Some devices need another way to connect. Enter a port number here to switch such an extra port on, or 0 or empty to switch it off.
conn.implicit: SMTP over TLS (encrypted from the first byte)
conn.legacy_warn: The listener without encryption sends passwords readable over the network. Only devices that are explicitly allowed on their Connection tab can sign in there. Leave it off unless you have a device that needs it.
conn.docker_hint: For the server administrator: a new port must also be published by Docker. Add these lines under ports: in the compose file (the first number is the port devices use) and run docker compose up -d:
conn.err_ports: Check the ports: numbers from 0 to 65535, and all different from each other and from the normal port.
conn.err_bind: The ports were saved, but a listener could not start: %s
conn.err_files: Choose both a certificate file and a key file.
backup.title: Backup and restore
backup.intro: Save the configuration of the relay to a file, or restore it, for example after moving the relay to another server.
backup.export_hint: Contains: all devices (name, addresses, username, password hash, on/off, rules) and the settings from this application. Does not contain: the Microsoft connection and its secret, the administrator password, the certificate and the log.
backup.sensitive: The file contains password hashes of your devices. Keep it private, like a password.
backup.import_hint: Devices are matched by name: existing devices are updated, new ones are added, devices that are not in the file stay as they are. The file is checked completely first; if anything is wrong, nothing changes. Afterwards enter the Microsoft connection again if this is a new installation.
backup.volume_hint: For a full copy (including the Microsoft secret, the admin password and the log) back up the Docker volume of the relay, which holds the database and the encryption key. Keep that copy private as well.
backup.err_file: This is not a backup file of this application.
login.code_error: That code is not valid. Try the current code from your app, or a recovery code.
login2fa.title: Verification code
login2fa.intro: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
login2fa.hint: Lost your phone? Use one of your recovery codes instead.
totp.title: Two-step verification
totp.intro: Adds a 6-digit code from an app (such as Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or a password manager) to signing in. Strongly recommended.
totp.setup_intro: Add this account to your authenticator app, then enter the code the app shows to finish.
totp.setup_hint: In the app choose to add an account manually and enter the secret key (time-based, 6 digits), or open the setup link on your phone.
totp.bad_code: That code is not valid. Check the time on your phone and try the current code.
totp.recovery_intro: Save these recovery codes now. Each works once if you lose your phone. They are not shown again.
totp.recovery_hint: Keep them somewhere safe and separate from your password, for example in a password manager.
security.title: Security
security.intro: Who can use this web interface, and from where.
security.add_hint: Administrators can change everything. Read-only users can look at all pages but cannot change anything. A generated password is shown once. Each user can add two-step verification under Account.
security.pass_once: Password for %s. It is shown only once.
security.allow: Only allow these networks to open this interface
security.allow_hint: For example 192.168.1.0/24. Empty = everyone who can reach the port. Your address now: %s. Saving a list that does not include your own address is refused, so you cannot lock yourself out.
security.session: Sign out after minutes of inactivity
security.err_session: The sign-out time must be between 5 and 480 minutes.
security.err_allow: Check the networks: addresses like 192.168.1.5 or 192.168.1.0/24, separated by commas.
security.err_lockout: Not saved: your own address is not in the list, so you would lock yourself out. Add it first.
flash.user_exists: A user with this name already exists.
flash.user_invalid: Check the username (letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore), the role and a password of at least 12 characters.
flash.last_admin: There must always be at least one administrator.
edit.mode_off_d: Nothing is checked. This is the default.
edit.mode_log_d: Mail goes through as normal. Violations are only written to the log, so you can see what would happen.
edit.mode_enforce_d: Mail that breaks the rule is refused.
